_meta.question: which #1947 roster models can colibri serve, and with which engine + quantisation
_meta.method: cross-check every roster row's HuggingFace config.json model_type against colibri's own family registry (c/family_registry.py), then confirm on the homeserver with the engine's own `coli doctor`
_meta.verdict: One roster model has a matching colibri engine and is already converted (qwen36 + int4-grouped gs64). Seven of the eight rows #3199's table marked 'runnable via an existing engine' have NO matching engine: their model_type is not in any of colibri's nine families. The correction is in the classification, not the tooling -- no new engine kernel was written and none is proposed here.
_meta.authority: colibri dispatches on the HF config `model_type` field. The set of model_types any family accepts is the whole compatibility surface; a checkpoint whose model_type is not in that set is refused by the engine, not merely unsupported by a converter.
_meta.converter_field_caveat: Only two of the nine families set the registry's `converter` field at all (glm53 -> convert_glm53.py, glm -> convert_fp8_to_int4.py). The other seven leave it empty, which per the registry's own docstring is not a gap: it means `coli convert` does not drive that family, either because its converter has a different command line or because it is not needed. The qwen36 row below is that case -- convert_qwen36.py is run directly with its own CLI. A null converter therefore never means 'unconvertible', and none of the verdicts here rest on the converter field.
_meta.engine_inventory: c/family_registry.py FAMILIES table, read verbatim. Local clone f028d26 (JustVugg/colibri); upstream dev re-checked 2026-09-27 and carries the IDENTICAL nine families and the identical model_type tuples, so nothing in this file is stale against upstream.
_meta.safetensors_only: colibri has no GGUF reader: `grep -rliE gguf c/*.c c/*.py c/tools/*.py` returns nothing in the source tree. Every roster artefact that exists only as GGUF (the requant ladder tags, the oversized-alias rows, the -GGUF mirrors) is therefore NOT a colibri input, whatever its architecture. Architecture-correct does not mean runnable; the artefact format decides.
_meta.homeserver: supermicro, NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada 20475 MiB, driver 615.71.09; clone at /var/benchmarks/colibri/src/colibri, venv /var/benchmarks/colibri/venv, containers /var/benchmarks/colibri/models
_meta.gpu_state_at_measurement: NOT MEASURED ON GPU, and the reason is load-bearing rather than incidental. The card had 18.4-20.1 GiB of its 20.475 GiB occupied by an unattended, in-flight #1947 phase-2 benchmark sweep (/tmp/matrix-p2.sh, 56/68 models done, 12 remaining, running since 2026-09-26) whose driver asserts a cold single-model protocol and had hp-llm-worker and ghidra-revdeck-1 stopped for its duration. Loading a colibri container would have put a second model on the card and on the host mid-measurement, and the CUDA kernel test allocates VRAM and could have OOMed the in-flight run. Neither was done. Every measurement recorded here is CPU-only and touched no VRAM: config fetches, registry reads, and `coli doctor` (which plans against free VRAM and allocates none).
_meta.no_scores: No benchmark score was produced, and none is copied or extrapolated. `coli doctor` validates a container; it is not the #1947 scoring harness. A per-cell score for any row below still requires a cold run through record_baseline.py, which is blocked on the sweep above.
_meta.doctor_verdict_caveat: `coli doctor` exits with 'result warning' rather than 'result ok' on the verified qwen36 container, and the warning is VRAM occupancy -- 'N GB of VRAM is already in use (only M GB free): this plan plans against the remainder'. Every content check passes. #3199's table calls this row 'doctor ok'; the accurate wording is 'container checks pass, placement plan computed against a contended card'. A placement plan derived from the wrong free-VRAM figure is not a placement plan, which is why the container verdict and the serve verdict are recorded as separate fields below.

qwen36.converter_invocation: c/tools/convert_qwen36.py driven directly with its own CLI (--model/--out/--gs/--low-disk/--no-mtp), not via `coli convert`

build_targets_present: All nine build targets resolve: `make -C c -n <target>` exits 0 for colibri, glm53, inkling, kimi_k3, olmoe, qwen36, qwen38, deepseek_v4 and deepseek_v41. Only four of the nine binaries exist on the homeserver (glm53, qwen36, qwen38, deepseek_v41); the `glm` family's own binary, c/colibri, does not, so the glm row below is unbuildable-then-unrunnable here for a second, independent reason.

summary.the_pair: engine qwen36 (c/qwen36, CUDA=1) + int4-grouped quantisation, ebits=4, expert_gs=64, on Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-abliterated
summary.correction_to_issue_3199s_own_split: Of the eight rows #3199's first table marked 'runnable via an EXISTING engine', one holds (Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-abliterated, qwen36), two are architecture-right but GGUF-only and so are pull/artefact problems rather than engine problems (qwen3.6-35b-a3b-dyn, ornith-35b-dyn), and five have no matching engine at all: GLM-4.6-reap-218b-dyn (glm4_moe), huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated, 0bserverx-Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic, qwen3.8-27b-dyn:q4_k_xl and glyphsoftware/sentinel-r3 (all dense qwen3_5), plus ravenx-chaos-agent-27b:Q4_K_M which the table also placed. The single most consequential finding is that the qwen38 family is not a Qwen3.8-27B engine: it accepts model_type qwen4_exp only, which is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B MoE with a 51B PLE table and no GPU backend. Naming it by brand rather than by model_type is what put five 27B dense rows in the runnable column.
summary.one_row_the_issue_missed: qwen3.6-27b-dyn:q4_k_xl (models_round7.txt line 15) is a dense qwen3_5 and therefore an engine gap, but it appeared in neither of #3199's two tables. The roster's 27B and 35B Qwen3.6 rows straddle the MoE/dense boundary the qwen36 family draws, so a ladder-level sweep is the only way to catch this class.
summary.pull_layer_detail: The two PULL_FAILED 27B rows and the gated sentinel-r3 are pull/licence problems: an ollama manifest that no longer exists, a 404 for config.json in a -GGUF-only repo, and a signed-licence gate (same wall as BaronLLM in #661). Each is recorded on its own row and none of them is counted toward the engine verdict, which is decided on model_type alone and would come out the same if every pull succeeded.
summary.new_engines_needed_but_not_written: dense qwen3 / qwen2 / qwen3_5, dense mistral + mistral3, gpt_oss, gemma, glm4_moe. Each is a new model_type in the family registry plus a hand-written engine and converter, which is #3199 option 2 and real work; this record classifies the gap and deliberately does not attempt it. The two dense-Mistral rows are not obviously one engine: mistral and mistral3 are different model_types with different architectures.
